biography: Victor Corrêa Filho, born under the scorching Brazilian sun in Ribeirão Preto, wasn't destined for the racetrack. His father, a cattle rancher, envisioned a future of vast fields and branding irons. But Victor, captivated by the roar of engines at a local karting track, secretly saved every spare real, spending weekends honing his skills. At 18, he sold his prized saddle to buy a battered kart, a move that nearly caused a family feud. His raw talent quickly became undeniable. He climbed the ranks, securing sponsorship from a local autoparts store, eventually finding himself piloting a Passat Classic FL. Despite flashes of brilliance, his inconsistency has plagued his career, leading to both spectacular victories and frustrating retirements. Now in his early thirties, Victor is at a critical juncture, battling to prove he can truly compete at the highest level.
drivingStyle: Victor's driving style is a volatile blend of aggression and finesse. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to take risks in corners, often pushing the car to its absolute limit. While this can lead to stunning overtakes and blistering lap times, it also makes him prone to errors and tire degradation. He struggles to maintain composure under pressure, sometimes cracking under the spotlight of a close race.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their karting days, fueled by contrasting driving styles and numerous on-track collisions.
A tense rivalry stemming from a controversial incident where Victor allegedly blocked Isabela during qualifying, costing her a potential pole position.
A professional rivalry born from battling for the same championship title, both drivers often trading paint and heated words.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of socks with a rooster pattern.
Listens to the same samba song before every race to calm his nerves.
Refuses to eat anything yellow on race days, believing it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed, it's about heart. And sometimes, a little bit of madness."
careerHighlight: Winning the Ribeirão Preto Grand Prix in 2018, his home race, with a daring last-lap overtake that sent the crowd into a frenzy.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the championship decider in 2020 while leading, handing the title to his rival, Ricardo Alves.
